instruments.title: Parents Bill of Rights Act
instruments.operative_summary: Sec. 401: as a condition of Dept. of Education funds, elementary and middle-grades-only schools must obtain parental consent before changing a minor's gender markers, pronouns or preferred name on any school form, or allowing a change of sex-based accommodations. Sec. 104 adds an ESEA parental 'right to know' if staff act to change a child's gender markers, pronouns or preferred name, and requires each school to notify the parents if staff take such an action.
instruments.operative_quote: shall be required to obtain parental consent before-- (1) changing a minor child's gender markers, pronouns, or preferred name on any school form; or (2) allowing a child to change the child's sex-based accommodations, including locker rooms or bathrooms. [Sec. 104 cl. (vii):] notifies the parents of any child who is a student in such school if a school employee or contractor takes, with respect to such child, any action described in clause (i) or (ii) of paragraph (1)(L).
instruments.rung_note: Sec. 401 = consent first (rung 5), but limited to changes 'on any school form' and to elementary/middle schools; coder must decide whether a school-form consent rule states rung 5's act (staff USE of name/pronouns). Sec. 104 also states rung 4 (notice duty). Bill states both 4 and 5; 5 is the stronger act.
instruments.status: passed House 2023-03-24; referred to Senate HELP 2023-03-27; died

instruments.title: Stopping Indoctrination and Protecting Kids Act (PROTECT Kids Act)
instruments.operative_summary: Sec. 2: as a condition of ESEA funds, a public school must obtain parental consent before changing an elementary or middle-grades student's gender markers, pronouns or preferred name on any school form, or sex-based accommodations. Sec. 3 bars ESEA funds for teaching gender ideology (from Owens' H.R. 2617). No separate notice duty.
instruments.operative_quote: a public school that receives funds under such Act shall obtain parental consent before changing a covered student's-- (1) gender markers, pronouns, or preferred name on any school form; or (2) sex-based accommodations, including locker rooms or bathrooms.
instruments.rung_note: Consent first, but scoped to 'on any school form' and to elementary/middle students - same scope caveat as H.R. 5 Sec. 401.
instruments.status: passed House 2026-05-20; referred to Senate HELP 2026-05-21; pending
sponsors: cosponsor on roster: Owens, Burgess (merged text includes his H.R. 2617; Owens' office calls it 'Owens Bill')

instruments.operative_summary: Sec. 3: as a condition of federal funds, elementary and middle-grades-only schools must obtain parental consent before changing a minor's gender markers, pronouns or preferred name on any school form, or sex-based accommodations.
instruments.operative_quote: shall be required to obtain parental consent before-- (1) changing a minor child's gender markers, pronouns, or preferred name on any school form; or (2) allowing a child to change the child's sex-based accommodations, including locker rooms or bathrooms.

instruments.title: Empower Parents to Protect their Kids Act of 2025
instruments.operative_summary: Sec. 3(b): no federal funds to a K-12 school unless staff (1) take no accommodation to affirm a student's identity incongruent with sex, or aid a minor in adopting it, without express parental consent; (2) do not encourage students to withhold that information from parents; (3) do not withhold or hide from parents information about a student's discomfort with sex or desired identity.
instruments.operative_quote: (1) School employees do not proceed with any accommodation intended to affirm a student's purported ``identity'' that is incongruent with the student's sex, or any action to facilitate or otherwise aid and abet a minor in adopting such an identity, ... unless the employees have received express parental consent to do so. ... (3) School employees do not withhold or hide information from parents about a student's discomfort with their sex, their desire for an identity that is incongruent with their sex
instruments.rung_note: Consent before any affirming accommodation = rung 5 (operative text does not name 'name' or 'pronouns'; those appear only in Findings Sec. 2(1)). (3) is a no-concealment rule, close to rung 4 but not an affirmative notice duty.
instruments.status: introduced 2025-09-03; referred to Senate HELP; pending
sponsors: Banks, Jim (LEAD SPONSOR - counts as Banks' own words)
cosponsors (none on roster): Cotton, Marshall, Scott (FL), Tuberville, Blackburn, Hawley, Moody, McCormick

instruments.title: Empower Parents to Protect Their Kids Act of 2023
instruments.operative_summary: Sec. 3(a): same structure as S. 2702 - no affirming accommodation or gender-transition action without express parental consent; staff may not withhold or hide information from parents about a student's desired gender transition or gender identity.
instruments.operative_quote: (1) School employees do not proceed with any accommodation intended to affirm a student's purported ``gender identity'' ... unless the employees have received express parental consent to do so. ... (3) School employees do not withhold or hide information from parents about a student's desired ``gender transition'' or a student's purported ``gender identity''
instruments.rung_note: As S. 2702. Lead sponsor Banks while a House member (federal; before his current Senate seat).
instruments.related: Banks also lead-sponsored H.R. 8170 (117th), same title (BILLSTATUS-117hr8170.xml fetched; text not read).

own_words.quote: Parents should never be kept in the dark about their own kids. This bill makes sure schools can't push radical gender ideology behind parents' backs and puts families back in charge where they belong.
own_words.note: 2025-09-03 release on S. 2702 (his lead-sponsored bill, consent-first). Quote alone states no act; it is anchored by the bill text. Release is Rep. Miller's, Banks named and quoted.

own_words.quote: Yet across the country, school districts are actively pushing radical gender ideology on children and, in some cases, facilitating social transitions without parental knowledge or consent. The Stopping Indoctrination & Protecting Kids Act is simple, any district that promotes these ideologies in the classroom or conceals a child's gender transition from their parents will lose federal funding.
own_words.note: 2026-05-20 official release on H.R. 2616 (also given as floor speech per Deseret/KSL). Describes the consent bill; 'conceals ... from their parents' language also leans to rung 4.

own_words.quote: Just last month, a New Jersey judge ruled to block multiple school districts from notifying parents of a child's gender identity change. Stories like these shouldn't become the new normal. That is exactly why House Republicans made commitments to address this problem and pushed for legislation that culminated in H.R. 5
own_words.note: 2023-09-14 op-ed (Fox News, reposted on official site). Implies support for notification policies; does not itself state the act. Possibly direction only - coder to decide.
